entry.title: GameCheck v1.0.0: GameCheck 1.0.0: free games and game sales in Discord
entry.content:
The first release of GameCheck: Free Game Check and Game Sale Check as one project, with a settings window and an import that sets everything up at once.

✨What it does

  • Free Game Check keeps one Discord message each for 🎁 free games, 🧩 free DLC & add-ons, 🎒 free loot, betas and in-game items, and 🧪 popular new demos. Steam and Epic Games are read straight from the stores, with exact end times for your country; Prime Gaming comes from LootScraper, IsThereAnyDeal adds more with your own key, and GamerPower fills the gaps.
  • Game Sale Check keeps one message for 🎉 the store-wide sales running now and coming up (Steam's seasonal sales and Fests, Epic, GOG) and one for 💸 the top deals per store, with price, regular price, discount and end.
  • Edited, not spammed. Every topic is one message, edited in place. 🆕 and 🔥 come and go on the minute, and a store that fails is replaced by its last good answer for up to 24 hours.
  • No timer to set up. The trigger Streamer.bot Started is enough: every run plans the next one itself.

🪟Settings window

  • The action [CG] - Settings opens it from its Test trigger. Its pages cover Discord (a bot or a webhook, one bot for both actions or one each), what is posted, the schedule, the platforms to leave out and the colours.
  • Status shows each action's last run and message ids, and has a Check now button.
  • Bot token, webhook URL and IsThereAnyDeal key are kept only in persisted global variables, never in the settings file, so an export carries no secrets.
  • Launcher links (off by default): Steam and Epic games open in Steam or the Epic Games Launcher instead of the browser.

🔧Already running Free Game Check or Game Sale Check?

  • Your Set Argument values keep working and win over the window, which shows them locked. Once the window has taken them over and you have saved, they can go.
  • Don't import over your existing actions: a second copy of each would post twice. Paste the new scripts into them and add only the settings action. The setup guide has the steps.

Import the attached GameCheck.sb, or paste the import string. To set the actions up by hand, the three scripts are attached as well. See the setup guide.

entry.title: Blackjack Game v16.3.1: A solo win posts its summary once
entry.content:
One chat fix for the solo game and two fixes for the settings window. BJG-Settings.json is read as it stands: no settings change, and there is nothing to redo after the update.

💬 Chat

  • A solo win posts its final summary once. When the dealer busted, when the player's hand was higher, or when the player won a tie-break, chat got the Final - {user}: … vs dealer … line twice in a row. Now it comes once, followed by the win message and the balance, in points mode and in free games alike. No message text changes.

🪟 Closing the window

  • The title bar's X asks before it discards. It used to throw away unsaved changes without asking. Now it asks the same question as Cancel, "Discard N unsaved changes?", and No keeps the window open.
  • A recompile or shutdown closes an open window. Streamer.bot recompiling the action or exiting used to leave the settings window up, still writing BJG-Settings.json from code that was no longer running. Now the window closes on the way out.

entry.title: Better Stream Announcements v2.1.1: GameVox and Stoat without Discord
entry.content:
Discord, GameVox and Stoat are now three delivery targets of their own, and Discord is no longer required: a GameVox or Stoat webhook alone is enough to announce with. The Setup Guide is rewritten for the new Settings window, with a screenshot of every page.

Import the new version over the old one; your settings stay as they are. Afterwards, check that Broadcaster Online and Broadcaster Offline are enabled if BsA announces your own stream: both come switched off in the import.

Changed

  • Discord, GameVox and Stoat each stand on their own. In v2.1.0 the GameVox and Stoat messages were copies that followed the Discord post, so they were only posted together with a new Discord announcement and a failed Discord post or edit held them back. Now each one is posted when a stream starts, updated while it runs, switched to its ended form when it ends, brought back with a stream that returns inside the revive window, and — for a Streamer Friend — deleted once Remove Old Message takes it down, whatever the other two are doing.
  • Discord is no longer required. A GameVox or Stoat webhook on its own announces your stream and your Streamer Friends. Home counts a channel as ready once any one of the three is set up, and Posting To shows GameVox and Stoat as targets of their own.

Fixed

  • Endless Stoat retries after the Stoat webhook was replaced. Stoat only lets a webhook edit and delete the messages it posted itself. A message from the previous webhook was asked about again on every cycle, forever; now it is let go after one warning and stays in the channel as it is.

Documentation

  • Setup Guide rewritten: every Settings page with a current screenshot, a table of the fifteen imported actions, and what ships switched off (the timers and Broadcaster Online/Offline).
  • FAQ: GameVox and Stoat, the Status Log, TikTok in /streamerfriends link, Reset to Defaults in the ☰ menu, and how the update check behaves.

Full details in the CHANGELOG.

entry.title: AutoBotCheck v1.1.0: AutoBotCheck v1.1.0
entry.content:
AutoBotCheck 1.1 adds the ISDS ban lists as a third source and makes later runs much faster: accounts that are already banned are skipped.

Import AutoBotCheck.sb over 1.0: TwitchInsight and TwitchBots.Info are replaced and ISDS.BanLists is added. Afterwards, check the group names in the Set Argument sub-actions if you changed them in 1.0: the import resets them to Bots and WhitelistedBots.

Added

  • The ISDS ban lists. The new ISDS.BanLists action bans the accounts on the ISDS Twitch ban lists. The isdsLists argument picks which of them are used.
  • Fast runs with the broadcaster token. Accounts are looked up 100 per request, and only the ones that are not banned yet are banned.
  • Your own people are protected. The broadcaster, the bot account, mods, VIPs and the whitelist are never banned. Nightbot, StreamElements and other hosted service bots are skipped unless they are in your bot group.
  • Wrong bans are undone. Service bots and your own accounts that AutoBotCheck banned are unbanned again. Bans with any other reason are never touched.
  • A dry run. With dryRun set to True the log shows what would be banned, and nobody is.

Documentation

  • Setup Guide: import, groups, arguments, running and stopping a check, protected accounts and the broadcaster token.
  • Import String to paste instead of the file.

Full details in the CHANGELOG.

entry.title: RhymeTime v1.1.0: An OBS overlay, set up and styled from the settings window
entry.content:
The round on stream. Import RhymeTime.sb over the old one — RT-settings.json and RT-wordbank.json are yours and stay where they are — then open [RT] - Settings and look at the new Overlay page.

📺The overlay

  • A browser source that shows the round: the word with its ending picked out, the countdown, the attempts left, and then the rhyme that won it and what it paid — or the rhymes that would have worked, after a lost one. A battle gets the same card in its own colour.
  • It ships inside the import. Nothing to download and no second file to keep up to date: the settings window writes the page out, and it listens to Streamer.bot's own WebSocket server (Servers/Clients → WebSocket Server, Auto Start ticked).
  • One button sets it up in OBS. Set the overlay up in OBS creates the scene and puts a browser source in it, the size of your canvas, pointed at the overlay. A source name OBS already knows is left alone rather than overwritten. By hand still works: Copy URL, then a Browser source with Local file unticked.
  • Try the demo plays sample rounds in your browser, which is the easiest way to place and size the source before anyone plays.
  • It stays off until you switch it on, and a round that reaches the card still says everything it says in chat.

🎨Yours to style

  • Where the card sits, how big it is, and how long a result stays up.
  • Switches for the ending pill, the attempt dots, the stake chip and the rhymes after a lost round.
  • Four colours — accent, battle, won and the card itself — with a picker behind each swatch and every lighter shade worked out from them.
  • All of it travels with the round, so a change is on screen the next time somebody plays and OBS is never touched again. The Browser source's own Custom CSS is read afterwards and still wins.

Nothing else about the game changed: the same commands, the same word banks, the same 19 chat lines.

Prefer pasting over downloading? The import string is the same thing. The Setup Guide walks through the Overlay page, and questions are answered in the FAQ.

entry.title: RhymeTime v1.0.0: The first release
entry.content:
The first release. Import RhymeTime.sb, enable the two commands, and open [RT] - Settings with a right-click on its Test trigger — the Setup Guide walks through it.

🎮The game

  • !Rhyme draws a word and gives the chatter a clock and a handful of attempts to rhyme with it. Answers go into ordinary chat — only the last word of the message is read, so "hmm maybe DREAM" counts.
  • Rhymes nobody listed still count. The rhymes you write are examples: the longest ending enough of them share becomes what the round accepts, so BAT, HAT, MAT takes any dictionary word ending in AT. A listed rhyme always counts, the target word never does, and a guess that does not even end the right way is ignored instead of costing an attempt.
  • Lines to finish. A target with spaces in it is a line to complete rather than a word to rhyme, and the whole reply has to match one of the answers you listed.
  • !RhymeBattle opens one word to the whole chat. The first valid rhyme takes the prize; nobody else pays anything. Moderators only, one battle per platform.

💰Points

  • A win pays the stake times the multiplier of the bank the word came from, a loss costs the stake, and a battle pays the moderator's stake or a flat reward. A battle nobody wins hands the stake back.
  • Chatters bet a number, or all, half, third, quarter, random, framed by a minimum and a maximum. Put the default bet at 0 and the whole game is free — nothing staked, nothing paid.
  • Currency Core by StreamUP and LOYALTY POINTS by tawmae are found on their own; the Game page is only for a points system of your own.

⚙️The settings window

  • Seven pages — Game, Battle, Word banks, Access, Messages, How to play, About — with Ctrl+1…Ctrl+7, Ctrl+S, light and dark, a count of what you changed and warnings about settings that cancel each other out.
  • A word-bank editor for the three banks, with Restore this bank for the words RhymeTime ships.
  • All 19 chat lines in one place, grouped by when they are sent, with clickable placeholders and a live preview of how each will read in chat.
  • Settings and word banks are written atomically: the previous copy is kept as .bak, and a damaged file is set aside as .broken instead of being overwritten.

🌐Everywhere

Twitch, YouTube and Kick all play, always, with the reply going back to the chat the command came from. There is no platform selection — restrict the commands in Streamer.bot instead.

Prefer pasting over downloading? The import string is the same thing. Questions are answered in the FAQ.

entry.title: Chat Calendar v1.0.1: Chat Calendar v1.0.1
entry.content:
A maintenance release: holidays no one greets each other for may now be left without a greeting, and the regions got a thorough going-over — Bavaria keeps Mariä Himmelfahrt, and every country with regional holidays brings all of its regions along.

✨Added

  • Greetings may be left empty. Not every holiday has one — nobody wishes a happy "Tag der Arbeit", and there is no customary greeting for Labour Day. Clear the Greeting on the Holidays page and nobody is greeted that day, while !holiday still answers with the name of the day and the announcement still lists it. An emptied greeting survives the next download and the change of year, like the ones you write. Your own holidays may be left empty too.

🐛Fixed

  • Mariä Himmelfahrt counts in Bavaria. date.nager.at lists 15 August for Saarland alone; it is a holiday in the Bavarian municipalities with a Catholic majority — nearly all of Lower and Upper Bavaria. Setup now adds the region after every download and to the holidays already written, cross-checked against openholidaysapi.org.
  • The Holidays page shows your region's holidays alone. It listed every holiday of the country, Bavaria's Reformation Day included, while the greeting, !nextholidays and the announcements had always left the others out. It now follows the region on the Calendar page before it is even saved, and the note under the list says how many of the country's holidays count where you are.
  • Every region of every country that has regional holidays, not Germany, Austria and Switzerland alone: all 50 US states, the Canadian provinces, the Australian states, the Spanish communities, the Italian regions and the rest — 259 regions in the 17 of 204 countries whose holidays differ by region. Every one is listed, not only those with a holiday of their own, so Florida and Lower Bavaria can be picked like any other. A country whose holidays never differ by region offers none.
  • Picking a region without a holiday of its own is no longer logged as a warning — most regions have none. Only a region belonging to another country is.

Import the attached ChatCalendar.sb, or paste the import string. The Setup Guide walks through every page. Your holidays, greetings and birthdays are kept: import over v1.0.0.

entry.title: OBS Notes v1.0.1
entry.content:
• The German chat answers are now standard German instead of Bavarian dialect.
  • The German command aliases are spelled out in full: !aufschreiben, !merken, !merkheft and !allesradieren replace !aufschreim, !merkn, !merkheftl and !allesradiern. Import the new version over the old one; the notes stay where they are.
  • Without Twitch, the Kick category picks the list: the live stream's category or, offline, the latest one, read from Kick's public channel page at most once a minute. When Kick does not answer, the last category stays; with neither Twitch nor Kick, the notes go to the list global as before.
  • Updates keep the post-its in OBS: the first command after an import points every browser source that still shows an older page (P&C Notepad's notepad_overlay.html, or one in another folder) to the current page and says so in the log. Before, the post-its stood still until the Test trigger ran, without a word in the log. The Test trigger takes such a source over instead of adding a second one.
  • The post-its hang like real ones instead of at two fixed angles: one of six angles (up to about 3 degrees left or right) or, for about one in four, straight, and never exactly like the post-it before it or the one it is stuck over. The pick comes from the note itself (time, author and text), so notes with the same text still hang differently, and each keeps its angle when OBS reloads the page.
  • More post-its than fit no longer disappear: the seventh is stuck over the first, the eighth over the second, and so on, a little off so the older ones peek out underneath. The line "+ N more" is gone.
  • New setting layout: vertical (two post-its side by side in three rows, 600 x 800, as before) or horizontal (three side by side in two rows, 900 x 560). The next command gives the browser source in OBS the new size; the Test trigger adds it in that size.

entry.title: Better Stream Announcements v2.1.0: Stoat & GameVox copies, a new Settings window and a color picker
entry.content:
Announcements can now go to GameVox and Stoat as well, the Settings window is rebuilt around a sidebar with a Home page and a Status Log, and every embed color gets a color picker. Nothing to redo after the update: the new webhook fields start empty, and while they are empty everything is posted exactly as before.

Added

  • A copy of every announcement on GameVox and Stoat. Broadcaster → Platforms and Streamer Friends → Platforms each take an optional GameVox webhook and an optional Stoat webhook. The copy follows the Discord message: updated with it and switched to its ended form when the stream ends. Your own announcement's copy also comes back with it within the revive window, and a Streamer Friend's copy is deleted together with the Discord message once Remove Old Message takes it down. It is only posted together with a new announcement, so a webhook added while someone is live starts with their next stream. Every call is best effort: one retry after a rate limit or a server error, a failure is logged, and Discord carries on either way.
    • GameVox gets the Discord post without buttons, role mentions and the embed timestamp, whose time moves into the footer (“LIVE since • 2026-10-25 20:15”).
    • Stoat (formerly Revolt) has no author line, fields or footer in its embeds, so the author line goes in bold above the embed and the fields and footer become lines of the description. No preview picture: Stoat only takes pictures uploaded through a bot account.
  • Home page: who is live right now and where announcements go, a five-step Start Here (can be hidden), today's warnings and errors at a glance, and help links.
  • Status Log page (Help → Status Log): everything BsA wrote to Streamer.bot's log, one day at a time, including the errors Streamer.bot reports about a BsA action. Filter by day, action, level and text.
  • Color picker on every embed color. A swatch beside each hex box shows the color; a click opens a picker right under the field — a saturation and brightness field with a hue bar to click or drag, sliders for red, green and blue (the mouse wheel nudges them by one), and the colors Discord uses most. Every change goes straight into the hex box, and typing a hex code moves the picker along.

Changed

  • The Settings window is rebuilt around a sidebar. The nested tabs are gone: the pages sit in four groups — Broadcaster, Streamer Friends, Discord Bot, Help — under the names they had as tabs. Ctrl+F searches every setting, the footer counts unsaved changes, Save (Ctrl+S) keeps the window open and Save & Exit closes it, and closing with unsaved changes asks first. Theme and reset sit in the ☰ menu.

Fixed

  • Placeholders for Owncast, Picarto, Rumble and TikTok friends. {user}, {title}, {game}, {url} and {viewers} came out as literal text, since these four only took %user% and the like. Both forms work now.
  • {game} on YouTube is empty instead of literal text, since YouTube gives no category.

Removed

  • The 🎨 button next to Random Embed Color, which only opened colorspicker.net; the picker beside each color replaces it.

entry.title: Chat Calendar v1.0.0: Chat Calendar v1.0.0
entry.content:
Twitch Calendar is now Chat Calendar: holiday and birthday greetings on Twitch, YouTube and Kick, a daily post to Discord, Stoat and GameVox, and one settings window for all of it. Nothing has to be run by hand any more — the window downloads the holidays itself.

✨Added

  • A settings window. Right-click the Test trigger of [CC] - .Settings and choose Test Trigger. Chat, Announcements, Calendar, Holidays, Birthdays, Messages and Log, with Help and About at the foot: every greeting with a chat preview, your own holidays and the greeting of every official one, the birthdays, the webhooks and the log of what was said and posted. It saves configs.json next to holidays.json; a damaged file is kept as configs.json.broken and the window falls back to the last save. A red pill in its header shows when a newer release is out.
  • YouTube and Kick. Chatters there are greeted on holidays and on their birthday, and every command answers in the chat it came from.
  • Birthdays. Viewers save their own with !birthday 24.12. (day and month only); moderators and you for others with !birthday @name 24.12.. Everyone is greeted once on their day, with {age} where the Birthdays page knows the year. !nextbirthdays lists the next ones.
  • Announcements. Today's holidays and birthdays go to Discord, Stoat and GameVox once a day, at the time you set — no Streamer.bot timer needed. A failed webhook is tried again after 15 minutes, without posting twice to the ones that worked. Title, lines and colour are yours, the colour with a picker.
  • Own days. Channel birthday, charity stream, anything: once on a date, or every year (12-24 or 24.12.).
  • Regions. Only the holidays of your region, if you pick one — Bavaria, Vienna, Zürich … — or only the nationwide ones.
  • Bot or broadcaster, and on Twitch as a /me message.

🔧Changed

  • No more Set Argument sub-actions. Every setting lives in the window. An argument of the same name in an action still wins, for a second action that should do something else.
  • Nothing to run by hand. .. Setup Action .. is now [CC] - Calendar Setup without a trigger: the window starts it when it opens without this year's holidays, after saving another country, region, time zone or year, and from Save and download now. A new year downloads itself.
  • Every chatter is greeted once per holiday, also when the stream runs past midnight, in the time zone you set.
  • All data lives in Chat Calendar next to Streamer.bot: holidays.json, birthdays.json, configs.json and a Logs folder kept for 30 days. Your own holidays and greetings survive every download.
  • Texts follow your country, or the chat language you pick; Boarisch writes Bavarian.

🐛Fixed

  • Holidays download again. date.nager.at dropped its CSV export; Chat Calendar uses its JSON API.
  • {holidayName} was empty, and two holidays on one day were announced as one.
  • The command answered nothing on a day without a holiday.
  • !nextholidays failed for countries without a translation (AT, CH, GB, PL …).
  • No more Hello @, without a user name, and no error in the log for every viewer without pronouns.

⬆️Updating from Twitch Calendar

Import over the old version. Your holidays (C:\streamer.bot\Twitch Calendar or Twitch Calendar next to Streamer.bot) are copied into Chat Calendar on the first run, with your own holidays and greetings; the country, region and time zone come along. Webhook URLs and your own texts from the old Set Argument sub-actions are entered once in the settings window. The commands ship switched off: enable them under Commands.

Import the attached ChatCalendar.sb, or paste the import string. The Setup Guide walks through every page.

entry.title: OBS Notes v1.0.0: Initial Release
entry.content:
First release.

  • Viewers save short notes with !note, read them back with !zettel; moderators and VIPs delete one with !radier <number> or all with !clearnotes. Every game (Twitch category) keeps its own list.
  • Twitch, Kick and YouTube: the answer goes to the chat the command came from, with an emote of that platform (Twitch and Kick global emotes, emoji on YouTube).
  • Post-its in OBS: the action's Test trigger adds the browser source OBS Notes to the current scene of the OBS connection named in AddOBSOverlayTo, and refreshes it when run again. The post-its follow every command within two seconds, size their text to the post-it, and make room for new ones by dropping the oldest.
  • Settings as Set Argument sub-actions: hideAfterMinutes fades the post-its out after a while without commands, colorfulNotes switches to black on white, showGameName puts the game name on the first post-it.
  • Chat settings: useBot answers from the bot or the broadcaster account, sendAsMe as a /me message, and language switches every answer and the post-its between German (partly Bavarian) and English.
  • Notes added at the same moment are all kept, and a crash while saving never leaves a broken file behind.
  • Times in chat are shown in the streamer's local time; a note too long for one chat message is shortened.

entry.title: Classic Chat Gamble v24.1.1: Damaged settings files are rescued instead of reset
entry.content:
A hardening release for the settings files. configs.json and messages.json are read as they stand — no setting changes, and nothing to redo after the update.

🐛Fixed

  • Damaged settings files are rescued instead of reset. A configs.json or messages.json that does not parse now falls back to the .bak copy beside it before the defaults, and the window says which file it read back from where. Until now a damaged file simply meant the defaults for everything it held, and the next save wrote them over it.
  • Every save leaves a .bak behind — the file as it was before that save, which is what the window reads back when the live one turns out to be damaged. A file that does not parse itself never becomes the backup, so a broken one cannot overwrite the last readable copy.
  • Free Game Mode and the bet it returns to afterwards are carried over from a configs.json rescued from its .bak; only one that cannot be recovered at all is left alone. Before, any damaged configs.json dropped them.
  • Only one settings window opens. A second trigger while it was up opened another one with its own copy of the settings, and whichever was saved last won. It now brings the open window to the front.
  • Switching pages refreshes only the page in front, instead of every control in the window.

Import the attached ClassicChatGamble.sb, or paste the import string.

entry.title: Blackjack Game v16.2.1: Atomic saves and a settings file that can be rescued
entry.content:
A hardening release for the settings file. BJG-Settings.json is read as it stands — no setting changes, and nothing to redo after the update.

💾The settings file

  • Saving is atomic. BJG-Settings.json was written straight over itself, so a crash halfway through could leave a truncated file behind — the game reads it on every hand. It is now written beside the live one and swapped in, and every save leaves BJG-Settings.json.bak, the file as it was before that save.
  • A damaged file is reported in the window and kept as BJG-Settings.json.broken. The window shows the settings from before the last save, or the defaults when there is no readable backup. Until now a read error raised an "Error loading settings" box from Streamer.bot's own thread — a modal dialog with no window behind it, holding the action until somebody found it — and then carried on with the defaults, which the next save wrote over the damaged file without a word.
  • A file that cannot be opened at all no longer opens the window. It said "damaged" and showed the defaults, so a save would overwrite a perfectly good file that was merely locked.
  • A settings file the game script is holding open is waited out instead of failing on the first try.

⏱️Cooldowns and the window

  • The cooldowns of !blackjack, !duel and !house were set from the settings window's own thread. All six are now handed to Streamer.bot's thread while the window is open, as one set, so they can never be applied as a mix of two saves.
  • Only one settings window opens. A second trigger while it was up opened another one with its own copy of the settings, and whichever was saved last won. It now brings the open window to the front.
  • Switching pages redraws only the page in front, instead of every control in the window.

entry.title: Battleship Game v2.0.0-pre-release.1: Chat vs the Admiral, Team duel & Click to Fire (pre-release)
entry.content:
[!WARNING] v2.0.0-pre-release.1 — the first test version of 2.0.0. It passes every automated check, but it has not run on a live stream yet. Try it on a test setup or back up your settings first, and please tell us what breaks. The stable version stays v1.0.0: the update notice in the settings window and the stable badge keep pointing there until 2.0.0 is final. Once it is, this test version's settings window shows the update notice for it.

📥 Install or update

  1. Back up <Streamer.bot folder>\Chat Games\Battleship Game\BSG-Settings.json.
  2. Download BattleshipGame.sb below and drag it into Streamer.bot's Import window — or open it in a text editor and paste its content as the import string. Click Yes on both messages.
  3. In the Commands tab, right-click the group [BG] - Battelship Game ▸ Enable All. The new commands arrive switched off.
  4. Open the settings: action [BG] - .Settings, right-click Test under Triggers ▸ Test Trigger.

No more Find Refs: the references in this import hold wherever Streamer.bot is installed.

Coming from 1.0.0? Your settings are kept; new settings start at their defaults. Going back to 1.0.0? Import its BattleshipGame.sb again. 2.0 has no platform switches, so tick YouTube and Kick again in the 1.0.0 settings if you use them.

The README and the Setup Guide on the main page still describe 1.0.0 until 2.0.0 is final — this page has everything for the test.

🧪 Please test

  • The import compiles — all three actions, no errors in Streamer.bot's log
  • The settings window opens, saves, and switches between dark and light
  • A solo battle: !battleship, !fire B7, !fleet, !board, running out of time
  • !seeschlacht: clicking on stream and !fire B7 both vote, and nobody wins or loses points
  • A team duel: !duel @name, !accept, !team A / !team B, the turns, and the payout to the winners
  • !stopbattle works for moderators and is refused for everybody else
  • The overlay set up with Set the overlay up in OBS (Overlay page)
  • Click to Fire with the Heat extension (Twitch)
  • Saving the game action or restarting Streamer.bot during a duel sign-up gives every entry back

Found something? Open an issue or write in the Battleship Game thread on the Streamer.bot Discord — with the command you used, what happened, and the lines from Streamer.bot's log.

✨ What's new

👥 Chat vs the Admiral — !seeschlacht

The whole chat is one fleet, played just for fun. Each round every viewer has one vote — a click on enemy waters or !fire B7 — and the square with the most votes is fired at. No points to win or lose, so every click counts, logged in to Twitch or not, with nothing to link first.

⚔️ Team duel — !duel, !accept, !team

One chat team against another. Challenge a viewer (or anybody), they accept, and everyone picks a side with !team A, !team B, !team <name> or plain !team. Every member pays the entry fee, the sides take turns voting on each shot, and the winners share the pot — their own entry back whole.

🖱️ Click to Fire (Twitch)

With the free Heat extension, the player whose battle is on screen fires by clicking a square in enemy waters right on the stream. The first click in a battle takes control; !fire link makes a link that lasts.

🛑 Moderator stop — !stopbattle

Ends whatever is running and pays nothing more out; a duel's entries are refunded. It comes set to the Moderators group.

🎨 A new settings window

In the look of the other Chat Games: ten pages in a rail (Game, Fleet, Modes, Overlay, Clicks, Access, Messages, Stats, Log, About), switches and segment bars, every chat message on one page with placeholder chips and a live chat preview, and a red pill when an update is out.

🌐 Every platform plays

The platform switches are gone. Twitch, YouTube and Kick always play, and every reply goes to the chat the command came from. To leave a platform out, untick it on the commands in Streamer.bot (for example Kick Message).

📺 Overlay v16

The duel's two sides, the chat's votes on the board, a countdown ring for every round, and no points shown in the chat's battle. The overlay reloads itself when the game installs a newer version.

🐛 Fixed

  • !board now comes with the import — 1.0.0 had no command for it.
  • The cooldowns set in the settings window reach the !battleship command; in 1.0.0 they went to a command that does not exist.
  • A cooldown message with {user} or any other brace was never sent. {user} works there now.
  • A payout, refund or charge never writes over a balance that could not be read.
  • Replies to !board and to votes go to the asker's own chat.
  • Closing Streamer.bot mid-game refunds every duel entry and fades the overlay out instead of freezing it.
  • A damaged BSG-Settings.json is reported and kept as .broken, instead of being reset on the next save without a word.
  • A battle starting while another one plays no longer takes the overlay away from it.

⚓ Commands

Command
!battleship Start a solo battle
!fire B7 Fire at a square, or vote for one
!fleet Redeploy your ships before your first shot
!board Shots, accuracy, ships left, running total
!seeschlacht Start Chat vs the Admiral
!duel @name · !accept · !team A Challenge, accept, join a side
!fire link Link your clicks on stream to you (Click to Fire)
!stopbattle Moderators: stop everything
!bstats · !ballstats Records and the leaderboard

The game knows its commands by their IDs, so you can rename any of them in Streamer.bot.

⚠️ Known limitations

  • Stopping everything when the action is saved again or Streamer.bot closes has only been tested outside Streamer.bot so far — it is on the test list above.
  • In the chat's battle a logged-out viewer can vote again by reloading the page. That is on purpose: it is played for fun.
  • Viewers on the Twitch app can't click — it shows no overlay extensions — so they vote with !fire B7.

entry.title: Hangman Game v12.0.0: Word Import, Blitz, Evil Hangman & Streaks
entry.content:
Added

  • Word import. An Import button on the Words page fetches words with hints from four free sources, shows them for review and adds the ticked ones to a category of your choice:
    • Wikidata (CC0): countries, capitals, big cities, rivers, mountains, chemical elements, musical instruments, sports, dog breeds, or any Wikidata class by its Q-ID. German or English, best known first.
    • OdeNet, the open German WordNet (CC BY-SA 4.0): animals, plants, food, objects, people & jobs, body, places, materials, nature and feelings, each with its German definition as the hint. Downloaded once and cached for a month.
    • PokéAPI: Pokémon names in German or English with their category as the hint, by generation.
    • IGDB: video game titles, best rated first. Needs the Client ID and Secret of a free Twitch developer app; both are kept in Streamer.bot's global variables, not in configs.json.
    • Words with digits or symbols, too many letters or too many words are skipped, accents are folded, umlauts can be written out, and a hint that names its own answer is replaced or masked. Difficulty is rated automatically from length, rare letters and how well known the word is, or set by hand.
  • Blitz rounds. Shorter time, fewer lives, and every point pays a multiplier. A round turns into a blitz by chance, or a mod calls one with !hm blitz. The overlay shows a pulsing BLITZ badge.
  • Evil Hangman. Once chat has lost a set share of its lives, the overlay glitches and the word is swapped. Every guess is wiped except one revealed letter, which the new word always contains. Lives either stay lost or refill, as you choose. At most once per round.
    • The glitch runs in stages slow enough to read on a browser source at a low frame rate: the old word breaks up, everything scrambles under scanlines with a blinking SIGNAL LOST, the new word decodes, and the surviving letter lights up in the accent colour. Its length is a setting (3 seconds by default, 0 for no effect).
    • Chat is told about the swap only once the glitch has played out. Until then guesses and !hmr are ignored and the "already running" reply stays quiet, so nothing in chat gives the new word away early. If the round ends meanwhile, the message is dropped.
  • Streaks. Each solved word adds to the solver's streak; it breaks when a round they guessed in is lost or times out. Winning streaks are announced, can pay a capped bonus, and show up as an extra line in the personal stats (!hmp). {streak} and {beststreak} also work in the board and stats messages, and the monthly reset clears them.
  • Seven new chat messages on the Messages page, under Blitz, Evil Hangman and Streaks.
  • Refresh Overlay in OBS button on the Overlay page. It reloads every OBS browser source that shows hangman_overlay.html.

Changed

  • The overlay is now version 9. It replaces the old file on its own and keeps it as hangman_overlay.html.v5.bak.
  • OBS keeps running the overlay page it loaded, even after the file on disk is replaced, so an update used to stay invisible until the browser source was refreshed by hand. The game now refreshes those browser sources itself over Streamer.bot's OBS connection after an update and once per Streamer.bot session, and the page reloads itself whenever a newer version is on disk.
  • A round ended with !killhm shows GAME OVER - MODERATOR STOPPED in orange on the overlay, instead of the red "GAME OVER - " of a lost round.

entry.title: Blackjack Game v16.2.0: A real shoe, a new settings window, OBS 33
entry.content:
🃏 A real shoe

Decks in the shoe and Reshuffle at finally do what they say. There is one shoe per platform, shared by every hand and duel running there. A played card goes to the discard pile and stays out until the shoe runs down to the threshold; then the played cards go back in and it is shuffled. Eight decks no longer play like one.

  • A card still in a hand is never dealt twice, even when the shoe reshuffles mid-round.
  • Change the deck count or the threshold and the next hand starts a fresh shoe.
  • A House table keeps its own shoe, sized by its rule set.

🎨 The settings window, rebuilt

Twenty-eight entries in six collapsible groups are now ten pages in a flat rail.

  • One Messages page for all 169 chat lines: pick a line, edit it, and a live chat preview shows how it reads.
  • How to play summarises the rules from what the window currently says.
  • The Log page filters by result, mode, platform and day.
  • Ctrl+S saves, Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+9 jump between pages, ⟳ resets one page, and the footer counts unsaved changes.
  • The colour wheel takes a click and a drag.

📺 The overlay and OBS 33

OBS 33 tightened how a browser source may read files from disk. The overlay now loads the table state as a small script file, so it works however OBS opens it: as a Local file, from a file:/// address or off a web server. It is version 13 and replaces an older copy on the next command, keeping that one as a .bak.

  • Set it up in OBS creates a 1300 × 1080 source.
  • The overlay catches up the moment OBS shows it, and says in the OBS log when it cannot read the state.
  • Amounts are grouped the way chat groups them (1.234.567).
  • A display name can no longer break the layout, in a hand or in the duel challenge prompt.

🔧 Fixed

  • Open stakes are paid back when Streamer.bot closes or the code is edited, instead of vanishing.
  • A maximum bet or hands-per-hour limit can be set back to no limit (0).
  • A 5-card Charlie and three sevens settle the moment they happen, doubling included.
  • !stats reports House Mode, and a full stats wipe clears the House figures too.
  • Kick viewers are booked to Kick, not Twitch.
  • all and the other bet shortcuts announce the stake the hand is actually played for.
  • The duel help named !duel; the command the import creates is !bjduel. A saved copy of that reply keeps its wording - reset it on the Messages page.
  • Quitting a seat returns its insurance stake; a player with a challenge waiting can no longer also take a seat.
  • Saving no longer trims spaces the chat lines rely on; three default lines no longer say @@username.

💬 Changed

  • Every chat line has been rewritten: same meaning, same placeholders, shorter.
  • The update check compares version numbers, so an older tag is never offered as an update.

🗑️ Removed

  • The platform switches. Streamer.bot already decides which platforms a command fires on; the game now answers wherever its commands fire. Channel points remain Twitch only.

Updating

Import BlackjackGame.sb below, or the import string, over the existing actions. Your settings and player statistics stay where they are.

entry.title: Trivia Game v8.0.0: New Gui, some fixes and QoL
entry.content:
Added

  • Settings window rebuilt as an icon rail — Game, Questions, Access, Messages, Log, How to play, About — with Ctrl+1-Ctrl+7 to switch and Ctrl+S to save.
  • Viewer suggestions: !Suggest question | correct | wrong | wrong, guarded by a channel point reward, Streamer.bot groups or mod status. A Suggestions page sets the guard, the category and difficulty they arrive under, the per-viewer cap, and whether they are playable at once.
  • Chat picks the category: !Trivia history, !Trivia 3 science, short forms like tv, movies, anime, maths. Only categories a round can be drawn from are offered; an unplayable name cancels the round rather than substituting another.
  • Messages page: all 63 chat lines behind one picker, placeholder chips, and a preview of the finished line including how it reads as a /me.
  • Difficulty dial: one slider for answer times, countdown reminders and spelling tolerance, Relaxed to Brutal. Every number stays editable; editing one switches the slider to Custom.
  • Header says what starts a round and whether the timer is on; footer counts unsaved changes.
  • Dispose() stops countdowns and closes the settings window when the action is destroyed, so a recompile mid-round no longer leaves the old build posting reminders.

Fixed

  • Channel point redemptions never started a round. A redemption carries a reward id and no command id, so it fell through to the answer handler. Start rewards are matched on the reward now — and the action needs a Twitch → Channel Point Reward Redemption trigger, which older imports do not carry.
  • Round ownership: skip, force end, a stale timeout and a blitz winner each claim the round before announcing, first claim wins. Fixes a last-second skip paying out anyway, force end announcing an end it did not cause, a skip racing a blitz winner, phantom "remaining rounds cancelled" lines, and a force end between two questions wiped out by the next round starting.
  • A round that threw while starting or resolving left that platform stuck on "a round is already active" until recompile, with its redemption neither refunded nor fulfilled.
  • The update check compared release tags as strings, so a build ahead of the latest release was told to update back to it. The notice is a header pill now, not a dialog in the way.
  • A question suggested from chat while the settings window was open was overwritten by the next save, a theme switch included. Saves fold in what arrived meanwhile; deletions stay deleted. Same for the addicted list against !TA.
  • A category holding fewer questions than the cache batch failed the whole round; the game asks for a single question instead of giving up.
